# 1 Clement Chapter 35 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal Equivalence)

**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Codex Alexandrinus, 1 Clement 35 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/1CL_035_page_001.jpg

---

## Chapter 35

**35:1** How blessed and wonderful are the gifts of God, beloved! Life in immortality, brightness in righteousness, truth in boldness, faith in confidence, self-control in holiness; and all these are within our comprehension.

**35:2** What then are the things prepared for those who wait for him? The Creator and Father of the ages, the All-holy One, knows their greatness and beauty.

**35:3** Let us therefore strive earnestly to be found in the number of those who wait for him, that we may receive a share of the gifts he has promised.

**35:4** But how shall this be, beloved? If our mind is fixed on God through faith; if we seek out what is pleasing and acceptable to him; if we accomplish what belongs to his blameless and upright will; and if we follow the way of truth, casting far from us all unrighteousness and wickedness, covetousness, strife, maliciousness and deceit, whispering and slander, hatred of God, pride and haughtiness, vainglory and want of hospitality.

**35:5** For those who practice these things are hateful to God; and not only those who do them, but also those who take pleasure in them.

**35:6** For the scripture says: "But to the sinner God said: Why do you recite my statutes, and take my covenant upon your lips?

**35:7** Yet you hated instruction and flung my words behind you. When you saw a thief you ran along with him, and you kept company with adulterers. Your mouth was full of wickedness, and your tongue wove deceit. You sat and spoke against your brother, and you laid a trap against your mother's son.

**35:8** These things you did and I kept silent; you thought, O wicked one, that I would be like yourself. I will convict you and lay the charge before your face.

**35:9** Understand this, you who forget God, lest he rend you like a lion, with no one to deliver you.

**35:10** The sacrifice of praise will glorify me, and there is the way by which I will show him the salvation of God."

---

*LOGOS preserves the formal structure of both Clement's vice-list (v. 4) and the Psalm 50 LXX citation (vv. 6-10), which is quoted here in an early LXX form.*
